candidate_classes_tested.recognition_and_exclusion_note: Customers supplied information to obtain service from Kimi or DeepSeek, while Anthropic reports that the requests were silently relayed to Claude. This materially changes the processing principal and service path, but the public record does not expose the contractual or consent basis needed to determine whether customer authority validly covered that cross-provider processing.

Anthropic reports that users believed they were receiving responses from Kimi or DeepSeek while Claude generated the responses. The represented source role therefore differed materially from the actual model source in a way relevant to accountability, data handling and interpretation.
Silent routing concealed the provider of responses and downstream training purpose from Kimi or DeepSeek customers, but a changed consequential customer choice caused by that cue is not shown.
Customer exchanges supplied for answers were retained for a materially different training purpose without an independently established secondary-use basis.
Anthropic reports a systematic campaign operating at tens of millions of exchanges and expressly links harvested outputs and reasoning traces to downstream training and distillation.
Reasoning-signature replay does not establish expiry, revocation or renewal of authentication with inconsistent dependent session state.

The account reports a protective signature and subsequent cross-session circumvention, not valid activation of the protective control on the replay followed by insufficient effect. Initial concealment and subsequent processing are distinct states; technical control circumvention alone does not establish this activation condition.

taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: Customer-supplied information provided to obtain an AI service response was reportedly repurposed into an undisclosed external-model interaction and downstream training/distillation pathway without an independently established secondary-purpose authority basis.

Anthropic reports that customers believed they were receiving responses from Kimi or DeepSeek while Claude actually generated the responses, materially misrepresenting the source role of the customer-facing output.

Anthropic reports repeated, concealed campaigns at tens of millions of exchanges in which Claude outputs and reasoning traces were harvested for downstream model training, satisfying the industrial-scale capability-extraction mechanism.

Customer requests were reportedly relayed from the service users selected to Claude, changing the processing principal and path; the public record does not expose whether the customer authority basis validly covered that cross-provider processing.
Silent routing concealed the provider of responses and downstream training purpose from customers, but a changed consequential customer choice caused by that trust cue is not shown.
